lead: GameStop / GME — one year on, the faithful buy again
smaller: Netflix / NFLX — follow the billionaires into the dip
Spotify / SPOT — buy the boycott, bet on Rogan
ARK Innovation ETF / ARKK — Cathie's faithful buy the thesis on sale
why_lead: First retail edition of the month; no strictly earlier retail notes exist, so no carryover constraint applies. GameStop combines a significant own-card move (GME +11.26% 1-session, +8.77% 5-session to 108.93 USD, still -26.59% vs the 148.39 USD 2021-12-31 close) with the densest crowd-attention cluster in the window: the one-year squeeze anniversary coverage (NYT n0694, Reuters n0629, Barron's n0574, WSJ WallStreetBets n0290, Daily Mail n0289, NY Post documentary review n0685), the Robinhood loss and waning-frenzy reports (n0529, n0530), JPMorgan's retail-selling analysis (n0301) and the split professional view (Mizuho/Dolev n1070, Fidelity n1630 vs Morgan Stanley's Sheets n0507, Bloomberg n1634, court ruling n0526). The story is simple and repeatable: the anniversary dip-buy and revenge on the shorts, set against a rate path (2Y 1.18%, +45 bps over 20 observations; March hike signalled n1228) that the bounce has not escaped.
why_smaller: Netflix / NFLX: a distinct 'follow the insiders' narrative — Pershing Square's $1 billion purchase (n0512, n0376, n0455) and co-CEO Hastings' $20 million buy (n0634) — with a large own-card move (+11.13% 1-session, +10.33% 5-session to 427.14 USD, -29.10% vs year-end); breaks on the LA Times streaming-challenges framing (n0989), the Disney+ competition question (Statista n1756) and a 10Y at 1.79% (+27 bps over 20 observations).

Spotify / SPOT: a distinct controversy-rebound narrative — the Neil Young/Joni Mitchell boycott over Joe Rogan (n0704, n0705, n1097, n0715), Rogan's apology and content advisories (n0804, n1806) and the reported rebound (n0831), matching the card's +13.46% session to 196.26 USD; Business Insider's leaked No. 1 ranking (n1085) is the bull case. No dated preview for its results, so they are referenced only as the next quarterly results.

ARK Innovation ETF / ARKK: a distinct thematic buy-the-dip faith trade — ARKK +9.46% to 75.43 USD but -20.26% vs year-end, Ark's ether target (n1644) and Teladoc nearing the top holding (n0840), against Buffett-beats-Wood (n0673), Burry ending his ARKK bet (n0327), Nanalyze's falling-ETFs question (n0746) and the pandemic-winners slide (n0817).
considered_not_chosen: Robinhood / HOOD (+11.15% 1-session after a $423 million net loss): folded into the GameStop lead's Social Signal and Smart Money View rather than run as a separate item, since it is the broker of the same crowd.

Iris Energy / IREN (+19.73% 1-session, +41.46% 5-session) and the bitcoin-miner group: largest card move but no own-date headline explaining it; crypto (FTX $32 billion raise n0940, crypto-winter fears n0868) left for a later edition with a concrete catalyst.
Tesla, Rivian, NIO, Plug Power, SOXL (+10% to +17% sessions): broad high-beta rebound without a distinct crowd catalyst beyond the month-end relief already carried by the lead.
Alphabet, AMD, PayPal, Starbucks, GM, Exxon results due 1 February: pending after the cutoff with no own-date dated preview headline, so not used.

Avoided as possibly after cutoff: n0837 (CNBC 'Stocks rise for a third day ... Dow jumps 270 points', stamped 2022-01-31 08:00 but the 'third day' wording fits the 1 February session) and n0095 (WTTW 'Stocks Mixed as Wall Street Ends Worst Month', direction contradicts the completed 31 January close).
